why: Multiple sources describe an affirmative solution: a conservative, ergodic, sigma-finite measure preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum was constructed via L1-flat {0,1} polynomials (arXiv:2210.15480, updated through 2023) and via rank-one flows (arXiv:2007.03684, 2020). Both predate the January 2024 snapshot, so this looks like a pre-snapshot resolution the list was not updated to reflect.

found.title: L1-flat polynomials and simple Lebesgue spectrum for conservative maps exist: A simple proof
found.note: Constructs a conservative ergodic sigma-finite measure preserving transformation with simple Lebesgue spectrum, answering Banach's problem affirmatively; last revised 2023.

found.title: On the spectral type of rank one flows and Banach problem with calculus of generalized Riesz products on the real line
found.note: Constructs rank one flows with Lebesgue spectral type, giving a positive answer to Banach's question for ergodic R-actions.
